title: Postmenopausal bleeding
claims: Postmenopausal bleeding is bleeding from the vagina after menopause; menopause is usually diagnosed in women over 45 who have not had a period for more than a year.
The NHS advises seeing a GP for any bleeding after menopause, even if it is only a small amount or has happened only once.
Postmenopausal bleeding is not usually serious, but it needs checking because it can be a sign of cancer.
A GP should refer a person with postmenopausal bleeding to hospital or a specialist clinic, and the NHS says they should not wait more than 2 weeks to see a specialist.

The most common causes include vaginal or endometrial atrophy, cervical or womb polyps and endometrial hyperplasia; ovarian or womb cancer is less common, and HRT is listed as a possible side effect rather than a most-common cause.
